course.title: BIO559R scRNA-seq Preprocessing
course.subtitle: A two-sample Scanpy lesson from 10x HDF5 counts to a reproducible preprocessing handoff
course.audience: Students with basic Python and introductory single-cell RNA-seq context
outcomes: Load and audit two compatible 10x Gene Expression HDF5 matrices.
Use per-sample diagnostics to make transparent preprocessing decisions.
Preserve raw UMI counts and save a reproducible preprocessing handoff.

modules.title: Preprocess Two scRNA-seq Samples
modules.question: Which cells and genes form a documented, quality-reviewed starting point for later analysis of two compatible scRNA-seq samples?

dataset.name: Two instructor-approved 10x Gene Expression HDF5 matrices
dataset.access_note: Students supply only approved, non-identifying matrices; original matrices remain unchanged.

modules.canonical_example: Two instructor-approved 10x Gene Expression HDF5 matrices
modules.decision: Choose and document whether each sample's QC distribution supports a minimum-gene rule and any additional sample-specific filters; make a separate doublet decision.
modules.diagnostic: Pre-filter and post-filter per-sample summaries and plots of total counts, detected genes, mitochondrial fraction, retention, and optional doublet scores.
modules.deliverable: A preprocessed H5AD object with raw counts preserved plus a JSON parameter/provenance record for a later analysis lesson.
modules.setup_code:
import anndata as ad
import scanpy as sc
import pandas as pd
modules.challenge: Change one documented QC threshold for one sample, predict the change in retained cells, and compare the post-filter diagnostic before retaining, narrowing, or withdrawing the filter decision.

solution_key.expected_reasoning: Students inspect each sample before filtering, preserve raw UMI counts in a named layer, avoid universal thresholds, and distinguish concatenation from batch correction.
solution_key.expected_evidence: A two-sample QC table/plot, explicit threshold dictionary, retained raw-count layer, and saved H5AD plus parameter JSON.
common_errors: Applying one unexamined threshold to both samples
Claiming that concatenation corrects batch effects
Adding PCA or clustering despite the lesson boundary
alternatives: Use no maximum-gene or mitochondrial rule until an appropriate diagnostic supports it
Record doublet scores without removing cells
Narrow the analysis claim when metadata or feature overlap is insufficient

rubric.evidence: Two compatible inputs, explicit labels, and a retained counts layer.
Per-sample diagnostics and a documented threshold/doublet rationale.
Version record, H5AD handoff, and JSON parameter file.
States that no batch correction, clusters, or cell identities were created.
